source.citation: R. K. Klein, J. O. Kephart, R. H. Pantell, H. Park, B. L. Berman, R. L. Swent, S. Datz and R. W. Fearick, Phys. Rev. B 31, 68-92 (1985)
source.method: Table III (p. 84) and Secs. II C, III transcribed from the Zotero full-text cache of attachment 3Q9K73K2; the PDF itself was not on disk at transcription time, and the Table I text layer is scrambled. Re-check against the PDF before pinning a test to these values.

crystal.type: natural IIa, free from nitrogen-platelet defects

beam.divergence_note: 16.9 MeV: about 0.6 mrad FWHM horizontally and 0.4 vertically (elliptical); 30.5 and 54.5 MeV: below 0.3 mrad FWHM. Plane orientation relative to the ellipse not stated.

detector.acceptance: 4.9 mm diameter Ta collimator about one third of the way to the detector; distances not given in the cached text, so a point forward detector is assumed.

analysis.fit: Background-subtracted spectra fitted with independent Lorentzian lines (Sec. IV); observed widths are the fitted Lorentzian FWHM of the detector-convolved spectrum.
analysis.theory: Calculated linewidth 1: quadrature sum of coherence-length (optical potential), multiple-scattering Doppler, Bloch and detector-resolution widths (Sec. II C). Calculated linewidth 2 adds a 0.9 um defect coherence length.
analysis.authors_conclusion: Calculated widths are much narrower than observed; widths observed with a synthetic diamond at 54 MeV are much narrower and in fair agreement with calculation, so the excess is attributed to incoherent scattering by defects with ~0.9-1 um spacing.

multiple_scattering_mrad.note: Authors' average in-plane multiple-scattering angle for 23 um (Eq. 22).

widths_table3.note: Column alignment of the cached text was checked by the energy/width/calc ordering of every row; Table I (energies and widths for all planes) supersedes Ref. 3 but is not transcribed because its cached text layer is scrambled.
